findings.description: The RDS MySQL instance sets storage_encrypted = false, so database storage, snapshots and automated backups hold the application's data (employee names and addresses) in cleartext on disk.

publicly_accessible = true gives the RDS instance an internet-routable endpoint, exposing MySQL beyond the VPC boundary to credential brute-forcing and direct exploitation; the endpoint is additionally published as a Terraform output.

findings.issue_category: plaintext master credentials and default username
findings.description: The master password is passed in as var.password (stored in cleartext in Terraform state and re-used verbatim in EC2 user data) and the master username is the well-known default 'admin', making guessing attacks against the public endpoint easier. Credentials should be generated and stored in Secrets Manager with managed rotation.

Neither the parameter group (no require_secure_transport) nor the application's mysqli_connect call enforces TLS, so credentials and query data can traverse the network in cleartext to a database that also has a public endpoint.

user_data interpolates the RDS endpoint, master username and plaintext master password into /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc. EC2 user data is readable from the instance metadata service by any local process or SSRF vector and via the EC2 console/API and Terraform state, leaking the database master credentials.

No metadata_options block sets http_tokens = "required", so IMDSv1 remains enabled. Combined with a PHP application processing untrusted POST input and a highly privileged instance profile, an SSRF or RCE yields both the role's temporary credentials and the user_data DB password.
No root_block_device with encrypted = true is specified, so the root volume - which stores the plaintext dbinfo.inc credentials file - may be created without encryption at rest.

The inline policy grants s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on Resource "*" to the EC2 instance role. Compromise of the internet-facing PHP application or theft of instance credentials via IMDSv1 yields full control of all S3 data, EC2 infrastructure and RDS databases in the account, including privilege escalation through actions such as ec2:RunInstances and rds:ModifyDBInstance.

Inbound MySQL 3306 is permitted from the entire VPC CIDR rather than only from the application server's security group, so any workload in any subnet of the VPC can reach the database directly. The rule is defined in aws_security_group_rule.catalog_db_inbound against this group.

The database security group permits all protocols and ports outbound to 0.0.0.0/0, allowing a compromised database host to exfiltrate data or reach arbitrary internet endpoints; no egress restriction provides defence in depth.

The instance runs a plain HTTP Apache/PHP application that collects user-submitted personal data (name, address) with no TLS termination configured anywhere in the configuration, and its public DNS name is exported as an output, so submitted data and session traffic travel in cleartext.
